headline: Monday's the window; break has slid off to Santa Rosa
body:
Today is a blowout — don't go. The triangle is running 8-plus feet with WNW gusting to 29 by mid-morning, and every zone from the channel to the outer waters is under a small craft advisory, Santa Rosa worse at 10-plus. Stay tied up.

Monday eases. The channel advisory lifts this evening, and inside the triangle seas drop to the 4-to-5-foot range on W wind 11 to 15, a workable day out of the harbor.

The problem is temperature. All three corners sit 70.8 to 72.2 — well warm of the 68 red line, so the cool side of the break is not inside the triangle at all. The 64–68 water has slid west to Santa Rosa Flats, which read 66.1 today and only soften to 69.1 Monday. But Santa Rosa stays rough — 7-plus feet, W to 25, and its advisory holds through Monday afternoon — so that run isn't worth it.

If you go Monday, start the triangle's cool west corner south of Santa Cruz, the 71.6 edge nearest the break, and work west.
